title: Finite-matrix refinement over one presentation member
statement:
theorem exists_condensedQbar_finiteFree_refinement
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : WeaklyEtale f)
    (P : CategoryTheory.Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X))
    (hP : Mod.IsFinitelyPresented
      ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} f).obj (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X))
      (((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} f).mapMod
        (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X)).obj P)) :
    ∃ C : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage Y, ∀ i : C.I₀,
      ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty
        ((CondensedRing.upperStar (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) (C.f i ≫ f)).obj P ≅
          Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) (C.X i)) r)

proof.text: Normalize the given finite presentation by extension of scalars along the canonical coefficient isomorphism. This sends regular modules and finite free modules to their corresponding modules and preserves cokernels. Import the canonical globalCoefficientIso from CondensedQbarFunctionCoefficients, where the finite-extension universe transport, normalization, diagram naturality and multiplicative filtered-colimit comparison are constructed once. Supply that isomorphism to the compatible function-presentation theorem to obtain C, fixed n,m, matrices M, fibrewise linear-cokernel equivalences, and presentations on each open. Quotient dimension plus range dimension equals n, so these linear equivalences give equal ranks. The matrix-refinement module no longer repeats the private coefficient construction.

source.place: Section 4, finite matrix refinement, coefficient realization, rank descent and maximal-minor elimination

proof.text: Each composite C_i to X is flat. For the union S of their images, flat going-down makes S stable under generalization and lifts every generalization at a point of C_i. Continuous matrix entries in the Hausdorff field have identical values at comparable points. Fibrewise rank agreement therefore descends the ranks to a specialization-invariant function on S. S is noetherian. To prove it quasi-sober, take the generic point in X of the closure of an irreducible closed subset of S: it generalizes a point of that subset, so belongs to S. Its closure in S is the original subset. There are finitely many irreducible components of S. A specialization-invariant subset is a finite union of the components it meets, so is closed; apply this to each rank level and its complement. Pulling these clopen levels back proves local constancy of each matrix rank.

source.place: Section 4, finite matrix refinement, coefficient realization, rank descent and maximal-minor elimination

proof.text: For each point choose a constant-rank open neighborhood and a nonzero maximal minor. Intersect with the nonvanishing locus of its determinant. The inverse determinant and block inverses stay in the same finite field, so are bounded continuous functions. Apply the proved Matrix.le_rank_map_iff, Matrix.schur_eq_zero_of_rank_le and Matrix.exists_eq_mul_fromBlocks_one_zero from the existing source library. Joint injectivity of point evaluation makes the Schur complement zero. This yields B = L diag(1,0) R with unit determinants. The proof includes rank zero and all empty matrix sizes without a separate positive-rank assumption.

source.place: Section 4, finite matrix refinement, coefficient realization, rank descent and maximal-minor elimination

proof.text: The ring homomorphism to endomorphisms sends matrix products to compositions in reverse order. A matrix with unit determinant gives an invertible biproduct map using its nonsingular inverse. The identity block is the projection onto the selected columns, a reindexing isomorphism, and the inclusion of the selected rows. Remove the epimorphic projection from its cokernel and identify the remaining cokernel with the complementary-row biproduct, reindexed by Fin k. Thus every chosen open has a genuine finite-free cokernel isomorphism. Assemble its Zariski cover and compose with C. The covering combinator is proved for an arbitrary property of a morphism, avoiding any reduction of the module pullback implementation. Empty schemes and empty fibres are covered by the same constructions.
